focus: Sembra che takes subjunctive (abbia) – impressions count as uncertainty even when they feel factual; anchor on this card's sembra che / abbia, drop the four-item trigger list.
Bisogna che + subjunctive – quote THIS card's 'Bisogna che il cuoco prepari', not the stock 'Bisogna che tu studi'; plain words, no 'impersonal necessity'.
Prima che + aumentino – 'before' clauses take subjunctive because the event hasn't happened yet; anchor on this card, drop the a-meno-che/senza-che list (dup on 2 cards, must differ).
'The most beautiful ever' takes subjunctive: il più bello che io abbia mai visto – lead with the surprise, not 'superlative relative'; fix 'piu' accent.
Voglio che + si sentano – Italian can't say 'want someone to do'; wants about other people need che + subjunctive. Cut the trigger list and 'signature features' fluff.
Questo libro, l'ho già letto – the fronted topic gets echoed by l', and the echo pronoun is required, not sloppy speech. No 'left dislocation'.
Sarà stato mezzanotte = 'it must have been midnight' – future tense as a guess about the past; lead with the surprise and fix the 'sara' accent.
Essendo stanco – a fronted gerund means 'since/because': 'being tired' = because he was tired. Plain words, no 'causal subordination'.
Non è che non voglia – 'it's not that I don't...' softens a denial and takes subjunctive; fix the 'Non e che' accent, drop 'negating a presupposition'.
Ne ha combinate di tutti i colori – literally 'pulled off ones of every color' = every kind of mischief. One rule: keep the idiom's literal logic, cut the 'partitive pronoun' lesson.
Non avendo ricevuto = 'not having received' – avendo + participle packs the earlier event into one clause, like English 'having done'. No 'compound gerund' lead.
Pur sapendo la verità = 'despite knowing the truth' – pur flips a gerund into 'although'. Anchor sapendo from this card (tip is duplicated on 2 cards, must differ); cut '(concessive gerund)'.
È auspicabile che + si trovino – bureaucratic 'it is hoped that', takes subjunctive; gloss auspicabile and fix the 'E' accent.
Arrivato a casa = 'once he'd arrived home' – a bare past participle can open the sentence, no 'having' word needed. Quote the card; no 'participio passato' lead.
Vale la pena sottolineare – literally 'it's worth the pain to underline'; standard academic emphasis formula. It's emphasis, NOT hedging – fix that.
Quanto più ci penso, tanto meno capisco = 'the more I think, the less I understand' – anchor the card's own quanto/tanto pair; drop the 'Più studio, più imparo' stock example.
È proprio questo che volevo dire – the è...che frame spotlights one element ('THIS is what I meant'). Plain words, no 'cleft sentence'; fix the 'E' accent.
Imparare una lingua = 'learning a language' – Italian uses the infinitive where English uses -ing as a subject. Lead with the English contrast, drop the circular 'functions as the subject'.
Sia che piova sia che splenda = 'whether it rains or shines' – both halves take subjunctive. Gloss it and give the hook; current tip is a naked fragment.
Di pazienza, ne servirà molta – 'of patience' fronted, then echoed by ne. Plain words, no 'topicalization'; different angle from the l' card (it-3424).
Il suo continuo lamentarsi – the infinitive works as a noun and takes il, suo, and adjectives: 'his constant complaining'. No 'nominalized infinitive' lead.
Letta la lettera – the opening participle AGREES with its noun (letta, feminine) and means 'having read the letter'. The agreement is the gem; cut 'implicit subject must match'.
Il vivere in città – Italian can put 'il' on an infinitive to make it a noun subject: 'living in the city'. Article angle (distinct from it-3596 and it-3640); no 'nominalized infinitive' lead.
